clause_text: The Tenant shall pay to the Landlord a security deposit equal to one month of the monthly rent upon signing this Agreement. The deposit is not to be used by the Tenant as payment of rent. At the end of the tenancy, the Landlord may deduct from the deposit any unpaid rent, utility charges, and the cost of repairing damage caused by the Tenant or the Tenant's guests, excluding fair wear and tear. The balance shall be refunded within fourteen days after the Tenant returns all keys and the Premises are handed over. If the Tenant renews the tenancy, the deposit may continue to be held under the new term unless the parties agree otherwise.

A security deposit of two months rent is payable before the Tenant moves in. The Landlord or the Landlord's agent will hold the deposit and may use it to cover any loss, damage, expense, or liability connected with the tenancy. The Tenant should note that the clause does not list the items that can be deducted, does not state when the refund must be made, and does not explain how normal wear and tear is treated. Any refund is subject to the Landlord's final assessment of the condition of the Premises and outstanding matters. The Tenant may wish to ask for a clearer written breakdown before signing.

The Tenant shall keep the flat clean and in good condition. The Tenant is responsible for minor repairs and maintenance up to a total of one hundred and fifty dollars per item, including replacement of light bulbs, tap washers, and small fittings. The Landlord shall be responsible for repairs to the structure, roof, main pipes, and electrical wiring, unless the damage is caused by the Tenant's misuse or negligence. The Tenant must report any defect to the Landlord or the Landlord's agent without delay. If the Tenant arranges a repair without prior approval, the Landlord may not be required to reimburse the cost.

The Landlord will maintain the air-conditioning units and arrange servicing every six months. The Tenant shall pay for all other repairs and maintenance within the apartment, including plumbing, electrical, window, and door repairs, regardless of the cause or cost. If the Tenant fails to carry out any repair, the Landlord may do so and recover the full amount from the Tenant. The clause does not state whether there is a cap on the Tenant's repair costs, how urgent repairs should be handled, or what happens if the repair is due to an old or defective fixture rather than the Tenant's act.

Either party may terminate this tenancy by giving at least one month written notice to the other party. If the Tenant terminates early without giving the required notice, the Landlord may deduct the rent for the notice period from the security deposit. If the Landlord terminates early, the Landlord shall refund the unused portion of any rent paid in advance, subject to deductions for outstanding charges. Notice may be delivered by hand or by registered post to the last known address of the other party. The parties agree that verbal notice alone is not sufficient unless later confirmed in writing.

This Agreement may be ended by either party after giving sufficient notice to the other. The notice period will depend on the circumstances and the parties shall discuss in good faith to agree on a handover date. If no agreement is reached, the Landlord may decide when the tenancy ends. Rent continues to be payable until the Tenant returns the keys and the Premises are vacated. The clause does not specify a number of days or weeks for the notice, does not say whether notice must be in writing, and does not explain how the deposit will be handled if the Tenant leaves before the agreed term.

Only the persons named in this Agreement may occupy the flat as regular residents. The Tenant shall not allow any other person to live in the flat, whether temporarily or permanently, without the Landlord's prior written consent. The Tenant shall not sublet the flat or any part of it, or assign this Agreement, without the Landlord's prior written consent. The Tenant must inform the Landlord or the Landlord's agent before any guest stays overnight for more than seven consecutive nights. The Landlord may require the Tenant to provide reasonable information about any proposed occupant, but the clause does not state how consent will be assessed.

The Tenant may have guests stay at the Premises for short periods, provided this does not disturb neighbours or breach any house rules. If a guest stays for more than thirty days in any six-month period, the Tenant must ask the Landlord for approval before the stay continues. The Landlord may approve or reject the request and may ask for additional rent or a higher deposit. The clause does not define short periods, does not say whether approval can be withheld for any reason, and does not explain whether the guest must be added to the agreement or recorded with any authority.

The monthly rent shall be paid in advance on the first day of each month by bank transfer or another method agreed by the parties. The Tenant shall pay all utility charges for the flat, including water, electricity, gas, and refuse charges, from the start date until the keys are returned. If any rent or utility payment is late by more than seven days, the Tenant shall pay a late charge of ten dollars per day until payment is received. The Landlord may apply any payment received first to outstanding late charges, then to utilities, and then to rent. The clause does not state whether the late charge is a penalty or agreed compensation.

The Tenant shall pay the monthly rent, the agreed maintenance fee, and any other charges stated in the schedule. The Landlord's agent may collect payments on behalf of the Landlord and may also charge the Tenant an administrative fee for each payment reminder or document request. The clause refers to miscellaneous charges but does not list them, does not state the amount of the agent's fee, and does not explain whether the fee is payable by the Tenant, the Landlord, or both. The Tenant may wish to request a written breakdown of all amounts before signing.

Upon signing, the Tenant shall pay a security deposit of one month's rent and the first month's rent. The deposit shall be held by the Landlord as security for the performance of the Tenant's obligations. The Landlord shall refund the deposit without interest within seven working days after the Tenant vacates the flat, provided all keys are returned, all utility bills are settled, and there is no damage beyond fair wear and tear. If there is any dispute about deductions, the Landlord may hold the disputed amount until the matter is resolved. The Tenant should ask for receipts and a joint handover check if possible.

The Tenant shall be responsible for minor repairs and maintenance costing up to two hundred dollars per job. This includes but is not limited to repairing leaking taps, replacing light bulbs, unblocking sinks, and fixing loose cupboard doors. The Landlord shall be responsible for repairs costing more than two hundred dollars, unless the repair is needed because of the Tenant's misuse, negligence, or failure to report the problem promptly. The Tenant must obtain the Landlord's written approval before arranging any repair that may cost more than two hundred dollars. Emergency repairs may be carried out first, but the Tenant must inform the Landlord within twenty-four hours.

If the Tenant breaches any term of this Agreement, the Landlord may terminate the tenancy immediately by giving written notice. The Tenant shall vacate the flat within seven days of the notice. The Landlord may also keep the security deposit and claim any additional losses, including legal costs and the cost of finding a replacement tenant. The clause does not give the Tenant a chance to remedy the breach before termination, does not define what counts as a serious breach, and does not state how the Landlord will calculate any additional losses. The Tenant may wish to clarify these points before signing.

Either party may terminate this Agreement after the first twelve months by giving two months written notice. If the Tenant terminates during the first twelve months, the Tenant shall pay the rent for the remaining period until a replacement tenant approved by the Landlord takes over the Premises. The Landlord may terminate at any time by giving two months notice if the Landlord or the Landlord's immediate family intends to occupy the Premises. The clause does not state how a replacement tenant is approved, whether the Tenant must pay any shortfall in rent, or what happens if the Landlord cannot find a new tenant.

The flat shall be occupied by the Tenant and such other occupants as may be reasonable from time to time. The Tenant shall not cause overcrowding or use the flat for any unlawful purpose. The Tenant shall not sublet the flat without the Landlord's consent. The clause does not state the maximum number of occupants, does not say whether children or relatives are included, and does not explain what reasonable means. It also does not say whether the Landlord's consent must be in writing or whether any fee is payable for adding an occupant. The Tenant may need to ask for these details separately.

The Tenant may sublet a room or part of the Premises only with the Landlord's prior written consent. The Landlord may refuse consent at the Landlord's absolute discretion and may impose conditions, including an increased security deposit, additional rent, or a requirement that the subtenant signs a separate agreement. The Tenant remains responsible for the whole rent and for any act or omission of the subtenant. The clause does not state whether the Landlord must respond within a certain time, whether any reason for refusal must be given, or whether the Tenant may use a professional subletting service. The Tenant should confirm the process before advertising any room.

The rent includes the usual utilities consumed by the Tenant, but the Tenant shall pay any excess over the usual amount. The Landlord or the Landlord's agent will determine what is usual based on previous bills and may adjust the amount from time to time. If the Tenant disputes the excess, the Landlord's calculation shall be final unless there is an obvious error. The clause does not state the monthly cap for utilities, does not show how the usual amount is calculated, and does not explain whether the Tenant can inspect the bills. The Tenant may wish to ask for a clear written formula before signing.

The Landlord's agent shall assist the Tenant with matters relating to the tenancy, including handover, repair requests, and communication with the Landlord. The agent may also provide advice on rent payment, utilities, and other matters from time to time. The clause does not describe the agent's duties in detail, does not state how quickly the agent must respond, and does not explain whether the agent has authority to approve repairs, refunds, or changes to the Agreement. The Tenant should not assume that any statement by the agent is binding on the Landlord unless it is confirmed in writing by the Landlord or someone with proper authority.

The condition of the flat shall be maintained and repairs shall be done as needed during the tenancy. The parties shall cooperate on any repair or maintenance matter. If a repair is required, the responsible party shall arrange for a suitable contractor and the other party shall allow access at a reasonable time. The clause does not state who is responsible for different types of repairs, does not set any cost limit, and does not say what happens if the parties disagree on whether a repair is necessary. It also does not explain how urgent repairs are handled if the responsible party cannot be contacted.

The security deposit may be used by the Landlord to cover unpaid rent, utilities, cleaning, repairs, or any other amount owed under this Agreement. The Tenant shall give notice of intention to leave by writing, and the Landlord shall confirm the final account after the Tenant vacates. The deposit balance will be returned after all deductions are agreed or determined. The clause does not state the notice period, does not set a deadline for the refund, and does not explain how disputes over deductions will be resolved. The Tenant may wish to request a move-in and move-out checklist with photos before signing.
